misconceptions.description: Treating an LXD choice as a matter of preference rather than a decision bounded by a named learner constraint
misconceptions.trigger: learner justifies a storyboard change with words like cleaner, nicer, or more modern instead of naming the constraint it resolves
misconceptions.feedback: An LXD decision is defensible only when it names the constraint it serves. Replace I liked it better with the learner need, the limit, and the evidence that the change addresses both.

misconceptions.description: Choosing a media or software feature before establishing the learning purpose it is supposed to serve
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds narration, animation, or a quiz widget and then reverse-justifies the learning goal
misconceptions.feedback: Sequence the decision as purpose first, media choice second, feature last. State the learner action the frame supports before defending the feature that delivers it.

misconceptions.description: Naming a course anchor such as cognitive load theory without letting it change any concrete design choice
misconceptions.trigger: learner cites Mayer or CLT in the rationale but the storyboard frame is identical to the version without the anchor
misconceptions.feedback: An anchor earns its place only if it changes wording, layout, timing, or feedback. Point to the exact frame element the anchor altered, or drop the citation.

misconceptions.description: Presenting a single final design as if no other defensible option existed, hiding the trade-off that makes it a decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner shows only the chosen frame and never records the rejected alternative or why it lost
misconceptions.feedback: A decision implies a road not taken. Record at least one rejected alternative and the constraint that ruled it out so a reviewer can audit the judgment.
